overview.summary: Tax consultants help people and businesses understand tax rules, file returns correctly and plan so they pay the right amount, no more and no less.
overview.problems: They help clients follow the law, avoid penalties and use legal reliefs and allowances they are entitled to.
overview.worksWith: Individuals, business owners, accountants, lawyers and tax authorities.
overview.workplaces: Accounting and tax firms, companies' finance teams and self-employed practice, mostly in offices.

timeline.title: Deadlines and priorities
timeline.description: The consultant checks upcoming filing dates and client requests.
timeline.why: Late filing can lead to penalties.

timeline.title: Reviewing documents
timeline.description: The consultant goes through clients' income records, invoices and receipts.
timeline.why: Accurate records are the base of a correct return.

timeline.title: Preparing returns
timeline.description: The consultant calculates tax and completes the forms.
timeline.why: Mistakes can cost money or cause disputes.

timeline.title: Advising clients
timeline.description: The consultant explains options and the effect of decisions, such as buying equipment or starting a business.
timeline.why: Clients decide better when they understand the tax effect.

timeline.title: Keeping up with the rules
timeline.description: The consultant reads updates to tax laws and notices from authorities.

timeline.title: Busy filing seasons
timeline.description: Around deadlines, hours can increase sharply.
timeline.why: Many clients file at the same time.

responsibilities: Advising on tax rules and planning within the law
Keeping up to date with changes
Representing clients with tax authorities where allowed
challenges: Peak seasons bring very long hours.
Rules are complex and keep changing.
Mistakes can cause penalties or disputes.
Clients may dislike the amount they owe or ask for improper shortcuts, which must be refused.
The work is detailed and repetitive.
Qualification and registration requirements vary by country.
workEnvironment: Mostly offices or remote work with computers and documents, with a strong yearly cycle. Hours are usually regular but long at filing deadlines. Some consultants work with individuals, others with companies.
tradeoffs: Pay and rules that vary by country

activity.title: Work out a pretend tax bill
steps: Invent a pretend person with a made-up yearly income.
Invent three simple tax bands, for example no tax up to a low amount, a low rate on the next part and a higher rate above that.
Calculate the tax step by step in a spreadsheet.
Check your answer a second way.
Write one sentence explaining the result to the pretend person.
activity.outcome: You practise applying rules step by step and explaining results clearly.
activity.safety: Use made-up numbers and made-up rules, never use real people's finances, and do not treat this as tax advice.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
